Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Expired controlled stock awaiting lawful disposition remains secured and accounted for.
A newly operating registrant records a zero initial controlled-substance inventory when no stock is on hand.
A pharmacist identifies whether an inventory was taken at opening or close of business.
A pharmacist estimates opened Schedule II stock because the bottle originally held fewer than 1,000 tablets.
A pharmacy preserves known or suspected theft-related surveillance for the longer applicable retention period.

stem: A pharmacy's DEA registrant wants a staff pharmacist to sign paper DEA Forms 222 when the registrant is away. The staff pharmacist is not the person who signed the pharmacy's most recent DEA registration application. Which arrangement can lawfully provide signing authority?

choices.text: A verbal instruction from the pharmacy manager made before each order, with no retained authorization record.
A notation in the pharmacy's employee handbook stating that every licensed pharmacist may sign Form 222 automatically.
Use of the registrant's CSOS password to sign the paper form electronically.
A supplier's written permission authorizing the staff pharmacist to sign the purchaser's order forms.
A compliant power of attorney granted by the registrant and retained so it is available for inspection.

stem:
A pharmacy purchases or transfers controlled stock between registrants. These are stock transactions, not patient prescription-information transfers. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The purchaser treats the ordered quantity as the final receipt record even when only part was delivered.
A pharmacy knowingly exceeds the distribution limit and waits until year-end to decide whether registration was needed.
A pharmacy distinguishes DEA Form 106 loss reporting from Form 222 ordering and Form 41 destruction records.
A pharmacy calculates the practitioner-distribution exception using dollars of pharmacy revenue.
A pharmacy considers the recipient’s familiar business name sufficient and omits the recipient-authority check.

stem: Before the next dispensing, a pharmacy orders Schedule II stock by an ordinary purchase order without Form 222 or CSOS. What is missing?

choices.text: Use the ordinary purchase order if the supplier also holds a DEA registration.
Use Form 106 because Schedule II stock is being acquired.
Use a DEA Form 222 or compliant digitally signed electronic order unless a specific exception applies.
Use Form 41 to document the incoming quantity.
Obtain prescriber signatures on the purchase order.

stem: A purchaser wants to replace paper Form 222 orders with electronic Schedule II ordering. What is required?

choices.text: Email a scanned Form 222 with an ordinary electronic signature.
Use the pharmacy's NPI as the CSOS signing credential.
Use CSOS software and a valid DEA-issued digital certificate.
Let any employee submit the order through standard purchasing software.
